description: Replacing variable, function, or other identifier names with alternative names while preserving program behavior.
typical_operators_or_tools: Random or scripted substitution; LLM-driven renaming (e.g., GPT-4)

description: Applying deterministic, non-learned structural or naming transformations drawn from an established tool or fixed transformation catalog, without invoking an LLM.
typical_operators_or_tools: CodePal AI Code Refactor; Pyrefact; Ruff; RopGen; MutableAST

description: Using a large language model to rewrite, refactor, or paraphrase the generated artifact while attempting to preserve its behavior or meaning.
Reformatting source code (whitespace, style) with a code formatter, without altering identifiers or logic.
Deleting, or excluding from the detector's input, the natural-language/comment portion of the generated artifact.
Truncating or removing a fraction of the generated artifact.
A battery of small, discrete edits: inserting statements or comments, modifying identifiers, I/O, literals, or assignments, or removing modifiable elements, applied individually or combined.
Rewriting code toward a more "natural" style with a dedicated naturalization model, aiming to obscure the stylistic cues the watermark relies on.
The attacker attempts to detect or localize the presence of the watermark itself, rather than removing it directly.
typical_operators_or_tools: ONION anomaly detection with CodeGPT; CodeBERTScore/CodeBLEU similarity analysis

description: A learned model, typically trained toward or with knowledge of the target watermarking scheme, is used to strip the embedded signal.
The attacker re-embeds a second, independent watermark, often via a surrogate model, over the already-watermarked artifact to overwrite or confound the original signal.
typical_operators_or_tools: Surrogate-model re-watermarking; independently trained second-watermark model

description: An attack specifically designed to remove signal carried redundantly across two independent embedding channels at once (e.g., naming and structural channels).
Broad structural perturbations that jointly target every structural channel used by a multi-channel embedding scheme.
Randomly corrupting a percentage of the sites or positions used to carry the embedded signal.
Applying several lightweight post-processing operations together (e.g., formatting plus renaming plus comment removal) as one combined condition.
typical_operators_or_tools: Combined formatting, renaming, comment removal, and normalization
